# zoneblick

> zoneblick is a self-hosted DNS zone watchdog, written in Rust. It resolves each zone from the root, asks every authoritative nameserver directly, checks the answers for correctness and risk, and reports what changed. It is open source and runs on your own server; it is not a hosted service.

Status as of 2026-11-13: early development. These things work: `zoneblick check <zone>` checks a zone once: delegation, nameserver consistency, DNSSEC (beta; signatures are not yet verified), mail policy (SPF, DMARC, CAA, MTA-STS, MX) and takeover exposure (dangling aliases, and aliases, mail servers or SPF includes that point into unregistered domains); `zoneblick run <zone> --name <name>` also collects the records of listed names and stores each run in a SQLite file; `zoneblick diff <zone>` shows what changed between two stored runs, per nameserver. `zoneblick serve` runs as a daemon from a TOML config file: it checks zones on a schedule, sends alerts by webhook, ntfy or email when something changes, and serves a JSON API and a web UI. All 26 checks of the v1 design are built, including aliases of unclaimed sites at eleven known hosting services (GitHub Pages, Amazon S3 and others, matched by signature), wildcard aliases, and nameservers in unregistered domains. `zoneblick run <zone> --discover ct` finds more names in Certificate Transparency logs through crt.sh; `zoneblick baseline pin <zone>` and `zoneblick diff <zone> --baseline` compare against a run pinned as correct; names whose addresses rotate are learned and not reported as changes; `zoneblick prune` and the daemon delete old runs (every run for 30 days, then one per day for a year). `--discover axfr` finds names by zone transfer where the nameservers allow it; `zoneblick findings mute <zone> <id>` silences an accepted finding; `zoneblick export --format json|csv` writes the stored findings; `zoneblick zones add|remove` edits the zones in the database. `zoneblick check <zone> --deep` (also `run --deep`, and `deep = "24h"` in the daemon's config) adds 11 deep checks: NSEC3 parameters, CDS/CDNSKEY consistency, algorithm completeness, EDNS compliance, open zone transfers, recursion on authoritative servers, query-name case, reserved nameserver addresses, and three SOA checks. Three deep checks (denial-of-existence proofs, key rollover state, all nameservers in one network) and DNSSEC signature verification are designed but not built yet. The current release is v0.8.0, an early pre-release. Each release has ready-built binaries on the GitHub releases page (https://github.com/cschweda/zoneblick/releases) for Linux (x86_64 and ARM 64-bit, static), macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel, unsigned) and 64-bit Windows (unsigned). There is an install script for Linux and macOS (`curl -fsSL https://zoneblick.com/install.sh | sh`) and a container image at ghcr.io/cschweda/zoneblick. It can also be built from source with a stable Rust toolchain (1.88 or later): `cargo install --git https://github.com/cschweda/zoneblick`. The name is always written in lowercase.

Key facts:

- Author: Christopher Schweda
- Language: Rust
- License: MIT or Apache-2.0, at your option
- Source code: https://github.com/cschweda/zoneblick
- It queries authoritative nameservers itself, over UDP and TCP, IPv4 and IPv6. It never trusts a recursive resolver's cache.
- It is meant for zones you control. It is not an offensive or scanning tool.

## Site

- [Home](https://zoneblick.com/): what DNS drift is, what zoneblick checks, how a run works, and how it differs from existing tools
- [Demo](https://zoneblick.com/demo.html): the planned web interface, shown with sample data only

## Documentation

- [README](https://github.com/cschweda/zoneblick/blob/main/README.md): how to try the `check` command, exit codes, and the JSON output format
- [Design document](https://github.com/cschweda/zoneblick/blob/main/DESIGN.md): goals, architecture, the full check catalog, data model and build phases
- [Decisions](https://github.com/cschweda/zoneblick/blob/main/DECISIONS.md): choices made during implementation, one line each

## Optional

- [Zonemaster](https://zonemaster.net): deep one-shot delegation and DNSSEC analysis; zoneblick does not aim for parity
- [DNSViz](https://dnsviz.net): DNSSEC chain visualisation
